Looking at the failing tests, I need to understand what's expected. The tests check for `class="math"` in the output. Let me analyze the patterns and rendering functions.

The `INLINE_MATH_PATTERN` uses `r'\$(?!\s)(?P<math_text>.+?)(?!\s)\$'` - this pattern uses a single `$` delimiter.

The `BLOCK_MATH_PATTERN` uses `$$` delimiters.

Looking at the test cases for block math (002, 003, 004) and inline math (001), and the `math_in_list`/`math_in_quote` tests which use `$$` for inline content within lists/quotes.

The issue seems to be with the `INLINE_MATH_PATTERN` - it uses single `$` but the tests might expect `$$` for inline math as well, or the pattern needs adjustment.

Looking at the `math_in_list` test: `'- $$\n  foo\n  $$\n'` - this should match block math within a list. The `math_in_quote` test: `'> $$\n> foo\n> $$\n'` - block math within a quote.

The `INLINE_MATH_PATTERN` with single `$` might be interfering. Let me check - the pattern `r'\$(?!\s)(?P<math_text>.+?)(?!\s)\$'` would match `$$` as `$` followed by `$` (empty text won't match due to `.+?`).

The real issue might be that `INLINE_MATH_PATTERN` needs to use `$$` for inline math to match the test expectations, or the pattern needs to not match inside block math contexts.

Looking more carefully at the test file references and the render functions - `render_inline_math` returns `$text$` but tests check for `class="math"` which is present. The `render_block_math` also has `class="math"`.

The `INLINE_MATH_PATTERN` should use `$$` delimiters to match the test cases for inline math (test_inline_math_001 likely uses `$$text$$`).
